Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:10:1.hebrew: מאן פייס - מי היה רשאי לקבל מעות:
Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:10:1.english: Who appeased? - Who was authorized to accept the money?

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:10:2.english: And who would forgo [it] - Who is the one in whose power it is to waive and forgive?

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:1:2.english: Korkor - Ravens, whose cry is similar to one who calls out "korkor."

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:1:3.hebrew: אפיק לי - כלומר, אל יקיזו לי עוד כאן, שעל כן העורבים באין:
Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:1:3.english: Remove [them] for me - That is, they should no longer let blood [from people] here on my account, for it is because of this that the ravens come.

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:2:2.hebrew: בבית הכסא - שעל גבי קרקע, ונראה לעינים, שכך היו בתי כסאות שלהן:
Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:2:2.english: In a privy - [A privy] that is on top of the ground, and is visible to the eyes, for this is how their privies were.

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:3:1.hebrew: מרחיקין השובך מן העיר - שהיונים מפסידין זרעוני גנות:
Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:3:1.english: One must distance a dovecote from a city - For the doves ruin the seeds of gardens.

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:3:2.hebrew: אא"כ יש לו כו' - שלא יפסידו היונים בשדה חבירו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:3:2.english: Unless he has, etc. - So that the pigeons will not cause damage in the field of his fellow.

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:3:3.english: The full range of a dove's flight - The distance of its flying course in a single flight.

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:3:4.hebrew: ואם לקחו - כמו שהוא, עם הקרקע. אפילו אין לו כל סביביו אלא בית רובע הקב, הרי הוא בחזקתו, שהרי הוחזק בו הראשון כן:
Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:3:4.english: And if he bought it - As it is, together with the land. Even if he does not have all around it [more than] a space of a quarter-kav [of sowing area], it remains in its presumptive status, since the first [owner] established the presumption in it [to be] so.

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:4:1.hebrew: אין פורסין נשבין - שלא ילכדו בהם יוני היישוב:
Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:4:1.english: One may not spread nets - so that they will not trap the doves of the settlement with them.

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:5:1.hebrew: וכרסייהו בחמשים אמה קמלייא - במה שהן מלקטין בתוך חמשים אמה, מתמלא כריסן, ואין מפסידין בזרעים מכאן ולהלן:
Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:5:1.english: And their stomachs are filled within fifty cubits - With what they gather within fifty cubits, their stomachs are filled, and they do not cause damage to the crops from there onward.

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:5:2.english: He may not spread - nets (nishbin, for trapping birds).

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:5:3.hebrew: ביישוב כרמים - שפורחין מכרם לכרם, ושטים הרבה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:5:3.english: In a settlement of vineyards - For they fly from vineyard to vineyard, and roam far and wide.

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:6:1.english: In a settlement of dovecotes - For [the pigeon] skips from one dovecote to another.

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:6:2.hebrew: ותיפוק ליה משום שובכין גופייהו - מאי מאה מיל דקאמר? דמשמע דבשביל יוני העיר מתרחק, שבאין כאן דרך שובכין. בלאו יוני העיר נמי לא יפרוס, שהרי לוכד יוני שובכות של אחרים:
Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:6:2.english: But let him derive it from the dovecotes themselves - What is [the point of] the "hundred mil" that it says? For it implies that he must distance himself because of the city's doves, which come here by way of the dovecotes. [But] even without the city's doves he should also not spread [a net], since he is trapping the doves of other people's dovecotes.

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:7:1.hebrew: טוענין ליורש וטוענין ללוקח - בית דין פותחים פה וטענה ליורש וללוקח שערער אדם עליהן, ויש לו עדים שהיתה שלו או של אבותיו, וזה אומר: ירשתיו מאבא, או: לקחתיו מפלוני, שהוחזק בו ימים רבים, והביא עדים שהוחזק בו אביו או המוכר לו שלש שנים, אע"פ שלא טען "והן לקחו ממך או מאבותיך" — טוענין לו בית דין ופותחים לו פה. ואילו למי שלא ירשה ולא לקחה מאחר, כשאמר לו המעורר: "מה אתה עושה בתוך שלי?" והוא אומר: "החזקתי בה ג' שנים ולא אמרו לי דבר" — תנא במתני' (לקמן בבא בתרא דף מא.) דאין לו חזקה. ומתני' דקתני "הרי הוא בחזקתו" אשמועינן דהיכא דלקחה מאחר ובאו וערערו עליו, אין צריך להרחיק. אלמא, טענינן ליה בשבילו, שאותו שלקחה ממנו (ונימא) נתפייס עם סביביו במעות עד שנאותו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:7:1.english: We argue [a claim] on behalf of an heir, and we argue on behalf of a buyer - The court opens its mouth and supplies a claim for an heir or a buyer when someone contests their ownership, and he (the challenger) has witnesses that it was his own or his ancestors'. The heir says, "I inherited it from my father," or the buyer says, "I bought it from so-and-so," and the property was held for many years, and he brought witnesses that his father, or the one who sold it to him, held it for three years. Even though he did not claim, "and they bought it from you or from your ancestors," the court argues on his behalf and opens his mouth for him. But in the case of one who neither inherited it nor bought it from another, when the challenger said to him, "What are you doing on what is mine?" and he says, "I held it for three years and no one said anything to me" — the Mishnah teaches (later, Bava Batra 41a) that he has no [established] possession. And our Mishnah, which states, "it remains in its presumptive status," teaches us that where he bought it from another, and [neighbors] came and objected to him, he does not need to distance [the dovecote]. Evidently, we argue on his behalf, [reasoning] that the one from whom he bought it appeased his neighbors with money until they consented.

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:8:1.hebrew: אינו צריך טענה - אינו צריך לומר: "אתה מכרת לאבי", אלא: "ראיתי לאבי שהחזיק בה, ולא ערער אדם עליו":
Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:8:1.english: He does not need a claim - He does not need to say, "You sold [it] to my father," but rather [he may say], "I saw my father holding it, and no one contested him."

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:8:2.english: He bought a courtyard that has projections - We learned in the Mishnah in [the chapter] Chezkat HaBatim: "One may not extend projections and balconies into the public domain." A person who builds a house may not extend the ends of its ceiling beams into the public domain. But if he wishes, he draws his building inward into his own [land], builds, and extends the ends of his beams outward. And if he bought a courtyard that has projections and balconies protruding into the public domain, it is in its presumptive ownership [chazaka]. For the court argues on his behalf that the first [owner] drew [the building] inward into his own [land], or that he reached a settlement with the public.

Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:9:1.hebrew: אימא לתוך שלו הוא כונס - שאילמלא כן, היו הרבים מעכבין עליו ולא היה יכול לעשות בזרוע. אבל כנגד היחיד, אימא בזרוע עשה, שהיה חזק ממנו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 23a:9:1.english: I might say that he is bringing [the produce] into his own [property] - For if not so, the public would have prevented him, and he would not have been able to act by force. But against an individual, I might say that he acted by force, because he was stronger than him.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:1:1.hebrew: אתו אומני ויתבי תותייהו - בקרקע שלהן היו יושבין, ולא בקרקע של רב יוסף, מדפריך בתר הכי: "והא גרמא הוא":
Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:1:1.english: "Craftsmen came and sat beneath them" - They were sitting on their own ground, and not on the ground of Rav Yosef, since [the Gemara] asks afterward: "But it is [only] indirect causation (gerama)!"

Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:2:1.hebrew: והא אחזיקו להו - פי' ר"י ב"ר מרדכי: כיון שלא בא להחזיק בקרקע של חבירו ולומר שלו הוא, אלא לתשמיש בעלמא שנהנה ממנה — מועלת חזקה שלא בטענה, דמסתמא לא היו אומרים שמכר להם רב יוסף תשמיש זה, והוו כי הנהו דלעיל (בבא בתרא דף ו.) דאחזוק להורדי, דמועלת חזקה שלא בטענה, דמדלא מיחה ג' שנים — מחל לו. ואין נראה, דאם לא הקנה לו, כי החזיק להורדי אמאי החזיק לכשורי? אלא על כרחך התם שטוען שהקנה לו, ולהכי אחזיק לכשורי, דאין אדם עושה קנין למחצה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:2:1.english: "But they established possession over them!" - Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Mordechai explained: Since he did not come to take possession of his fellow's land and to say that it is his, but only for a mere usage from which he benefits, a possession without a claim is effective, because presumably they would not say that Rav Yosef sold them this usage. And they are like those cases above (Bava Batra 6a) where they took possession of the hurdai, [where we hold] that a possession without a claim is effective, since he did not protest for three years, [which shows] he waived it. But this does not seem right, for if [the owner] had not transferred it to him, then when [the person] took possession of the hurdai, why did he also take possession of the keshuri? Rather, you must say that there he claims that [the owner] transferred it to him, and that is why he took possession of the keshuri, for a person does not make a partial acquisition.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:2:2.hebrew: אין חזקה לנזקין - אומר ר"ת: דאפי' הקנה יכול לחזור בו, דקנין בטעות הוא — דסבור היה שיכול לקבל, ועכשיו אין יכול לקבל. ואין נראה, דמדקאמר "אין חזקה לנזקין" איכא למידק: הא ראיה יש, כדדייקינן בחזקת הבתים (לקמן בבא בתרא דף מט:) גבי הא דתנן: "ולא (לאשה חזקה בנכסי בעלה)":
Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:2:2.english: There is no chazakah for damages - Rabbeinu Tam says that even if he had transferred [the right], he can retract, for the transfer was made in error — he thought he could tolerate [the damage], and now he cannot tolerate it. But this does not seem [correct], for from the fact that [the Gemara] says "there is no chazakah for damages," one can infer that if there is [explicit] proof, [the right is established], as we inferred in [the chapter] Chezkat HaBatim (below, Bava Batra 49b) regarding that which we learned in the Mishnah: "And not (does a wife have a chazakah in her husband's property)."

Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:2:3.hebrew: בקוטרא - נראה לר"י דדוקא בקוטרא דכבשן, שהוא גדול ומזיק ביותר, אין חזקה, כדאמר במרובה (ב"ק דף פב:): אין עושין כבשונות בירושלים. מ"ט? משום קוטרא. ודוקא נמי בית הכסא שלהן, שהיה למעלה מן הקרקע והיה מסריח ביותר; אבל בשלנו, שהוא מכוסה, יש חזקה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:2:3.english: Regarding smoke - It appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak that specifically with the smoke of a kiln, which is large and exceptionally harmful, there is no chazakah [of permitted usage], as it says in [the chapter] Marbeh (Bava Kamma 82b): "They do not make kilns in Jerusalem." What is the reason? Because of the smoke. And likewise, [the ruling that there is no chazakah] applies specifically to their latrines, which were above ground level and gave off an exceptionally foul odor; but in the case of ours, which is covered, there is a chazakah.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:2:4.hebrew: לדידי דאנינא דעתאי - פי' שהיה איסטניס, כדאמרינן בערבי פסחים (פסחים דף קיג: ושם): שלשה חייהם אינן חיים — הרחמנים, והרתחנים, ואניני הדעת. אמר רב יוסף: וכולהו איתנהו בי:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:2:4.english: "For me, since my mind is delicate" - Meaning, that he was fastidious (istenis), as we say in the chapter Arvei Pesachim (Pesachim 113b, and there): Three [types of people] — their lives are not life: the compassionate, the hot-tempered, and those of delicate mind. Rav Yosef said: And I have all of them.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:2:5.hebrew: כקוטרא ובית הכסא דמו - והא דקאמר "אפיקו קורקור מהכא", משמע דמשום עורבים היה אומר; ודאי אם לא היו עורבים היה סובל, אף על גב דאנינא דעתיה. אי נמי, העורבים היו אוכלים הדם ופורחים ומקנחים בפירות:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:2:5.english: They are like smoke and a privy - And as for what [Rav Yosef] said, "Remove the kurkur from here," this implies that he was speaking because of the ravens. Certainly, had there been no ravens, he would have put up with [the bloodletters], even though his mind was distressed [by them]. Alternatively, [the problem was that] the ravens would eat the blood, fly off, and wipe themselves on the fruit.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:3:1.hebrew: מרחיקין השובך מן העיר חמשים אמה - מפני התבואה הנשטחת בגגות העיר כדי לייבש. אבל לתבואה שבשדות ליכא למיחש בקרוב לעיר, לפי שהשדות רחוקין מן העיר אלף אמה, כדתנן (ערכין דף לג:): אין עושין מגרש שדה, ולא שדה מגרש:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:3:1.english: "They distance a dovecote from the city fifty cubits" - Because of the grain that is spread out on the rooftops of the city in order to dry. But as for grain in the fields, there is no concern [about doves] near the city, since the fields are a thousand cubits away from the city, as we learned in a Mishnah (Arakhin 33b): "One may not make a [city's] open land into a field, nor a field into open land."

Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:3:2.hebrew: ולא יעשה שובך תוך שלו - ברחוק מן העיר, בין השדות. ואצטריך למיתני תרוייהו: דאי תנא רישא "להרחיק מן העיר" — התם דוקא מרחיק, מפני שתבואות העיר מגולות הן, בחצר הן בגג; אבל תבואה הנזרעת בשדה ומכוסה, אין צריך להרחיק. ואי תנא סיפא — משום דבשדות שכיחא תבואה; אבל בעיר דלא שכיח כולי האי, אימא לא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:3:2.english: "And one may not make a dovecote within his own [property]" - [This refers to a location] far from the city, among the fields. And it was necessary for [the Mishnah] to teach both [rulings]: For if it had taught only the first clause, [that one must] "distance [a dovecote] from the city," [one might think that] there specifically one must distance it, because the grain of the city is exposed, whether in the courtyard or on the roof; but grain that is sown in a field and is covered does not require distancing. And if it had taught only the latter clause, [one might think it applies] because grain is common in the fields; but in the city, where [grain] is not so common, I might say [that the restriction does] not [apply].

Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:3:3.hebrew: בית ארבעת כורין כמלא שגר היונה - ור' יהודה ורבנן לא פליגי בשגר היונה כמה הוי, דמודו רבנן דבית ארבעה כורין הוי שגר היונה. אלא רבנן סברי: כיון דבחמשים אמה מליא כריסייהו, כדאמרינן בגמ', תו לא מזקי טפי; ור' יהודה סבר דכמלא שגר מזקי:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:3:3.english: "A area of four kor [of land], [which is] the extent of a dove's flight" - Rabbi Yehudah and the Rabbis do not disagree about how much constitutes "a dove's flight," for the Rabbis agree that an area of four kor is [the extent of] a dove's flight. Rather, the Rabbis hold: Since within fifty cubits they fill their bellies, as we say in the Gemara, they no longer cause greater damage [beyond that distance]; whereas Rabbi Yehudah holds that [the doves] cause damage [as far as] the full extent of the flight.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:4:1.hebrew: אלא אם כן הרחיק שלשים ריס - היינו ד' מיל, דהמיל ז' ריס ומחצה. ופעמים שהגמרא נותן שיעור בריסין, ופעמים במילין, ופעמים בפרסה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:4:1.english: "Unless he distanced [it] thirty ris" - That is, four mil, for a mil is seven and a half ris. Sometimes the Gemara gives the measure in ris, sometimes in mil, and sometimes in parsa.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:5:1.hebrew: והתניא ביישוב אפילו מאה מיל - תימה: דמאי ס"ד דהוי פי' "וביישוב" אי קרי העיר "יישוב"? א"כ אפילו מאה מיל לאו דוקא, כמו שמשמע, אלא אפילו אלף מיל או יותר; א"כ בשום מקום לא יפרוס, אפילו במדבר ורחוק לאין סוף מן העיר! ואפילו אם נאמר דמאה מיל דוקא, מכל מקום היאך יפרש את הברייתא? דהכי תניא בתוספתא דמרובה: "אין פורסין נשבין ליונים, אא"כ הרחיק מן היישוב שלשים ריס. בד"א במדבר, אבל ביישוב אפי' מאה מיל לא יפרוס", כיון דעיר קרי יישוב. ואי ס"ד דהכי פירושו: "בד"א במדבר" — פי' שאין זרעים, "אבל ביישוב" — פי' ביישוב זרעים, "אפילו מאה מיל לא יפרוס" — אם כן, מאי קשיא ליה? ואומר ריצב"א: דודאי ס"ד דאיירי ביישוב זרעים, ולהכי פריך: "ומישט שייטי שלשים ריס ותו לא?" אפי' ביישוב זרעים, והא מוכח דביישוב זרעים שייטי טובא, ואין זה אלא משום אכילה; אלמא דלא מליא כריסייהו בחמשים אמה. ומשני: דלא איירי ביישוב זרעים, אלא ביישוב שובכין ויישוב כרמים, וקרי "מדבר" היכא דליכא שובכים וכרמים:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:5:1.english: "But it was taught: In a settled area, even a hundred mil" - This is puzzling: What was the thought that "settled area" [in the baraita] would mean that the city itself is called a "settled area"? If so, "even a hundred mil" would not be precise, as it implies, but rather even a thousand mil or more; then one would never be allowed to spread [a dovecote net], even in a desert and infinitely far from the city! And even if we say that a hundred mil is precise, in any case how would one explain the baraita? For so it is taught in the Tosefta of Bava Kamma (chapter "Marbeh"): "One may not spread nets for pigeons unless he distanced himself thirty ris from the settled area. When does this apply? In a desert; but in a settled area, even a hundred mil he may not spread," since a city is called a "settled area." And if it were to enter one's mind that this is its meaning — "When does this apply? In a desert" — meaning, where there are no crops, "but in a settled area" — meaning, a settled area with crops, "even a hundred mil he may not spread" — then, what was the difficulty for [Abaye]? And the Ritzba says: Certainly it entered [the Gemara's] mind that the baraita speaks of an area settled with crops, and therefore it asks: "But do [pigeons] fly only thirty ris and no more?" even in an area settled with crops; and it is proven that in an area settled with crops they fly much farther, and this is only for the sake of eating; so evidently they do not fill their bellies within fifty cubits. And [the Gemara] answers: that [the baraita] does not speak of an area settled with crops, but of an area settled with dovecotes and an area settled with vineyards, and it calls it a "desert" wherever there are no dovecotes and vineyards.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:8:1.hebrew: יורש תנינא - וס"ד המקשה דמתני' אשמעינן ביורש, וה"ה בלוקח. ומיהו רב זביד דנקט נמי יורש, אמתני' דלקמן סמיך; אבל מתני' דהכא לא שמעינן מינה יורש, מדאיצטריך מתני' דלקמן:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:8:1.english: "An heir – we have already learned [this]" - And the questioner assumed that the Mishnah [here] teaches us about an heir, and the same applies to a buyer. However, Rav Zevid, who also mentioned an heir, relied on the Mishnah below. But from the Mishnah here we do not learn [the law of] an heir, since the Mishnah below was needed [to teach it].

Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:9:1.hebrew: וצריכי - וא"ת: ביורש נמי ליתני תרתי? וי"ל: דאשמעינן בלוקח, וה"ה ביורש:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:9:1.english: "And they are needed" - And if you ask: Regarding an heir too, let [the Mishnah] teach two [cases]? And one can answer: [The Mishnah] teaches us [the principle] regarding a buyer, and the same applies to an heir.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:9:2.hebrew: אחולי אחילו גביה - פי': ז' טובי העיר במעמד אנשי העיר שהרשות בידם, כדאמר פרק בתרא דמגילה (דף כו.). וכיון דליכא לכל חד בדרך אלא פורתא, מחלי טפי מיחיד:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 23a:9:2.english: "They surely waived [their rights] regarding it" - Explanation: [The waiver was made by] the seven elders of the town, in the presence of the townspeople, since they have the authority [to do so], as stated in the last chapter of Megillah (26a). And since each individual has only a small portion in the road, they waive [their rights] more readily than an individual does.
